correctness.rationale: On the three-dimensional null-filiform associative algebra e1²=e2, e1e2=e2e1=e3, torsion basis equations force N=[[a,0,0],[b,a,0],[c,d,a]] over any field. Since e1 generates A, every algebra automorphism is determined by φ(e1)=u e1+v e2+w e3 (u≠0), giving φ=[[u,0,0],[v,u²,0],[w,2uv,u³]] and conjugation (a,b,c,d)↦(a,ub,u²c+v(2b−d),ud). Generic [b:d] projective directions allow c elimination; the exceptional direction d=2b has invariant τ=c/b² and a surviving affine modulus. For b=d=0, nonzero square-classes of c produce gcd(2,q−1) orbits; q generic directions and q exceptional values, giving q(2q+1+gcd(2,q−1)) classes over Fq. Independent sympy conjugation plus COMPLETE action orbit census for q=2,3,5 reproduced 12,27,65, respectively. General theorem follows algebraically, not by induction from small q.
